text:
The best matching future climate location is Whitman County, WA, which has a strong match quality with 8 out of 8 climate models in agreement. Lower sigma means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Regarding rotations, 1 matching area uses the field's current rotation, which is a flexible mix of pulses, spring wheat, winter wheat. The matching places also use a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, winter wheat, as well as winter wheat to spring wheat to fallow, and winter wheat to spring wheat to pulses.

For hazards compared to the best match, Whitman County has 31 hot days above 32 degrees Celsius per year compared to 18 for the field today. It has 191 frost-free days compared to the field's 150 days. For soil water in the driest month of September, the match has 21.1 percent compared to 16.6 percent for the field today.

Under high emissions, temperatures and precipitation will change across the year by the 2050s.

These results come with candidates based on 3351 farmland cells at approximately 4 kilometers using the Cropland Data Layer.
